Phoenix Signal

Build: 2026-09-29 · GPT-6 Astra Pro · my-3D2dge v0.6.0

Launch

Open this HTML directly in a recent browser. No connection, installation, server, assets folder, or build step is needed. Press Enter or choose Deploy. Browser audio starts after a gesture. Landscape orientation is recommended on phones. Settings, checkpoint, mission progress, scores, and survivor correspondence use local storage, when the browser permits it for local files.

Mission

A complete, condensed rescue mission interpreting Fallen Memory, the power-plant mission from Burning Rangers (Sega Saturn). The mission has an entry, connected search sectors, two authorization rescues, coolant restoration, a damaged crossing, purge terminals, a fire-flower reactor encounter, an extraction route, results, and survivor correspondence.

Fidelity boundary: This is an original playable interpretation, not a verified room-for-room reconstruction. A complete authoritative first-mission walkthrough or original map was not successfully retrieved. The checklist below therefore distinguishes verified source systems and setting from authored placements. It does not assert that every original Fallen Memory rescue placement, room, or story event is present.

Additions and modernizations

Original title, sector names/layouts, survivor names and letters, three readable memory records, mission text and radio script. Independent movement/aim/jump/dodge controls. Optional aim assistance and offscreen route beacon, no minimap. Explicit rescue energy choice. Perfect-evade bonus and modest slow motion. Adjustable effects and quality. Sector checkpoints and local resume. Post-hit recovery supply of three crystals. Custom orthographic camera with quarter turns, rather than a Saturn perspective camera. Reactor attack timings and mission objective gates are new balancing choices.

Outside the slice

The other three Saturn missions, underwater movement, later bosses, original cinematics, whole-game secrets/passwords, original survivor randomization and the 3,125-layout replay system, full email collection, original maps, and original recorded performances are outside this mission interpretation. No swimmer or inactive menu entry is presented as a finished feature.

Audio manifest and credits

Every score, effect and spoken phrase is registered in the single AUDIO manifest. Four original synth placeholders (launch, interior, reactor, home) take structural direction from the source's energetic title/action and restrained radio-led exploration; they are not note-exact arrangements. Effects are original synth approximations: select, confirm, shot, charge, charged, quench, gem, jet, step, land, dodge, perfect, whistle, blast, hit, break, shield, transport, radio, terminal, deny, enemy, exposed, lift, alarm, victory. The 32 speech clips are original offline eSpeak en-us+f3 synthetic PCM placeholders. They are not Sega voice samples. They use the same effects/master/mute buses as the engine synth. No sampled music or source SFX were redistributed.

Original game and characters: Sega / Sonic Team. Source music reference: Naofumi Hataya, Fumie Kumatani and Masaru Setsumaru as credited in the source game's documentation. The Zophar archive was used as a soundtrack catalog reference; no claim of transcription or audio-identity fidelity is made. Procedural art and mission implementation: this build. Engine: my-3D2dge, Michael Crosato, MIT, supplied by the user. eSpeak software is used only as an offline authoring tool; no executable or runtime is bundled. Speech output is original generated dialogue.

Known limitations

Orthographic 3D staging does not reproduce the original behind-the-back perspective. Geometry, enemy patterns, characters' appearance, rescues and story sequencing are adapted, not exact. Music/SFX are source-style placeholders rather than verified transcriptions. Spoken guidance is synthetic rather than the original cast. High-quality WebGPU depends on browser and graphics support; Canvas remains the default. Browser local-file storage rules vary. Phone play is best in landscape. Physical gamepad and target Samsung/RTX hardware performance have not been measured. Visual stunt transform keeps small face/accessory offsets upright.

Hub migration notes

The first engine script is unchanged. The game lives in a separate strict IIFE with const E = My3D2dge;. The HTML contains no Emberdeep game code. Hub removal is limited to the engine block and shell, then shared-engine loading.

  1. E.Audio.prototype.playPCM / stopPCM: optional engine extension for cached embedded PCM playback, one voice at a time, stereo pan, engine effects/master buses, and node cleanup. Needed because the engine exposes a chip synth but no public embedded sample player. It uses _init and sfxBus; a public shared sample API would replace these internals.
  2. E.applyRigFlip: optional post-pose 3D joint transform for the evasive somersault. Uses the Humanoid J joint collection, including blade direction. Needed because stock rig input has no somersault parameter. A future public rig root-orientation API would be preferable.
  3. E.Input.prototype.touchButtons wrapper: tracks each button pointer until window pointerup/cancel or blur. The stock node-only release can leave an action held when a scene or modal replaces its button before release. This additive fix prevents stuck touch actions. The shared hub should give input instances an explicit disposal lifecycle for these listeners, as for the stock engine listeners.
  4. World drawing uses E.px and renderer queues/actors/decals/overlays; characters remain rigs. No raw arc, stroke or fillText calls appear in the game. Static map texture callbacks return RGB. Game-specific ground wrapper supports pits, collapsing bridge and moving lift atop E.Body/E.TileMap. E.Bullets handles projectile motion; game collision checks include height. E.SpatialHash narrows targets.
  5. DOM outside engine: fullscreen on #stage, restyling the returned engine touch buttons, pointer-to-pixel menu hit testing, and this scrollable documentation panel. No external fonts/images/audio/network. Normal gameplay and menus are pixel-rendered.
  6. Save keys: ps:options, ps:run, ps:checkpoint, ps:last, ps:best, ps:mail through E.store (which adds its own my3d2dge prefix). Four E.songs keys and all custom SFX begin ps:. Global read-only-inspection getters are exposed on window.PhoenixSignal for QA; they expose mutable object references but no player-facing cheats.
  7. Own modal pause freezes mission simulation while UI remains responsive; game.paused is not used. Engine audio levels/ducking follow the worked example's private helper pattern. WebGPU is requested only via Options, after support and adapter checks. Quality Auto uses measured frame time with hysteresis; High vs Balanced changes particle cap, fire-light count, ambient detail and GPU shadow settings.

Validation

Final automated mission pass, 2026-09-29: Chromium reached the results screen after all six sectors, with 8/8 survivors, 3/3 memory records, 76 fires suppressed, the reactor defeated, and extraction complete. That pass recorded 09:05 mission time, rank A, score 50,608, 33 perfect evades, and 39 hits. The full pass used a virtual standard gamepad, path steering, actual shots and interactions, and the same 1/120-second engine simulation. It did not grant mission resources, teleport the player, set objective flags, or bypass the boss. Browser page errors: 0. Console warnings/errors: 0. game.errors: [].

Additional checks passed: keyboard movement and air boost; camera rotation and return; radio PCM playback; mute; pause freezing the mission timer; options and diagnostics; High/Balanced particle and lighting-budget changes; unavailable-WebGPU fallback; opening/closing the embedded report; five-crystal rescue; saving to title and continuing with the same rescued survivor and crystals; results correspondence, letter reading, and reopening saved mail from the title. A separate failure fixture set one life and no crystals, then used fire contact to test failure, blocked Escape dismissal, and checkpoint retry. That fixture was not used in the full completion pass.

Landscape mobile emulation (844 × 390 CSS pixels, touch enabled, device scale 3) verified the engine move stick, JET/SHOT buttons, touch pause/resume, and removal of held actions after replaced buttons. The touch pointer-release fix is in the separately labeled extension block. Other repaired issues included Enter selecting pause-menu entries instead of dismissing the menu, rear gates obscuring the player at deployment, a blocked gate landing, bridge collapse timing, spent boss shockwaves, and preservation of uncollected normal crystals across saves.

Test boundaries: The lab browser blocks both file:// navigation and local HTTP navigation by policy. Tests loaded the exact delivered HTML with Chromium's in-memory page-content API, without runtime network requests. Direct double-click launching was therefore not observed here. Save/continue and correspondence were tested through a Storage-compatible in-memory shim because that injected page has no usable native origin storage. Real local-file persistence remains browser-dependent. Real requestAnimationFrame smoke tests also ran. Physical controllers, target Galaxy/RTX hardware frame rates, actual WebGPU rendering, and every browser's fullscreen behavior were not measured; no hardware-specific 60-fps guarantee is claimed.

The original engine block was compared with the uploaded core and is unchanged. SHA-256 of its UTF-8 script text: 1e3e3107508f389cabd660ccd821445c92096b9931408a57846233da637d7ec3. All assets are inline. Documentation links are optional credits; gameplay performs no fetches or downloads.
